title: Park a cell on a question and answer it
action: Add two cell verbs per contract decision 16031715 (D1 b7b5b3c7, D2 8ed6f4a2). Park record shape: one append-only array trace.park; each entry {question, parked_at, answer, answer_decision, answered_at}; the open question is the last entry with no answer. `bee cells park --id <cell> --question <text>` sets an open or claimed cell to status `parked`, appends a park entry, releases the cell's claim (clear the claim fields and trace.worker the way release does) and every file reservation the cell holds, adds NO attempts row, and passes guard_claim_ownership like block does (with --force-ownership). It refuses an empty question or a cell that is capped, dropped or already parked. `bee cells answer --id <cell> --answer <text>` refuses a cell that is not parked; otherwise it logs the answer as a decision BEFORE it writes the cell (tags `cells` and `slp`, both already in docs/decisions/taxonomy.json, the way dissent.rs does, so the taxonomy file never changes; the decision text names the cell id and quotes the question and the answer), appends the new decision id to the cell's `decisions`, stamps answer, answer_decision and answered_at on the open park entry, and sets status `open`. Answer needs no claim ownership: the claim was released at park. A failed decision log leaves the cell unchanged. Every refusal on a parked cell names the remedy `bee cells answer --id <cell> --answer "<text>"`. In schedule.rs `classify`, add a `Some("parked")` arm so a dependent of a parked cell is excluded the way a dependent of a blocked cell is (today classify reads parked as pending and the in-degree count skips it, so the dependent lands in wave 1). In handlers_close.rs, `bee cells reopen` refuses a parked cell, naming the answer remedy. Copy the shape of `run_block` / `block_cell` in handlers_close.rs (rg anchor: `"block" => run_block(flags, use_json, t0),` in util.rs) and of `record_dissent_verdict` in dissent.rs for log-then-write. audit.rs `log_decision` returns no id today (`pub(crate) fn log_decision(root: &Path, decision: &str, rationale: &str, tags: &[&str]) -> MR<()> {`): add a variant that returns the id; keep the old signature for its callers. Register both verbs in the util.rs try_mutating match AND in generated/registry_payload.json (the registry tests fail if a served verb is undeclared). The registry file is hand-edited (no generator exists): edit it by a JSON round-trip that keeps its compact byte format. Also export, through `mod park; pub(crate) use self::park::*;` in cells/mod.rs, a reader `feature_parked_cells(root, feature) -> Vec<(cell id, question)>` shaped like `feature_dissent_debt` (it reads live and archived cells) for cqp-2 and cqp-4, and a helper `park_answers(cell) -> Vec<(question, answer)>` for the brief. Check the existing status checks for a status they now meet: handlers_write.rs `let status_ok = matches!(cell_map.get("status"), Some(Value::String(s)) if s == "open" || s == "blocked");` and `if status != "open" && status != "blocked" {` — a parked cell must not be claimable and must not be updatable into a running state; leave them unchanged unless a test shows a parked cell slips through. Tests red-first: park sets status and question and frees the claim and reservations; a parked cell is absent from compute_schedule's waves while its open sibling is present; a cell that depends on a parked cell is absent from every compute_schedule wave AND from ready_cells; answer logs a decision, cites it on the cell, stamps the park entry and reopens it; reopen refuses a parked cell; the refusals named above each name the answer remedy. REWORK after judge (NEEDS_REVISION): (a) block_cell has no parked guard, so `bee cells block` then `bee cells reopen` turns a parked cell open with the question unanswered — refuse block on a parked cell naming the answer remedy; (b) unclaim on a parked cell points at reopen — name the answer remedy instead; (c) claim on a parked cell (handlers_write.rs) must name the answer remedy, with a test that asserts the text, not only is_err; (d) answer logs the decision inside the mutate closure before write_cell, so a failed write leaves an uncited decision — log only after every check that can refuse has passed, as close to the write as the log-then-write rule allows, and name the residual case in the cap; (e) supervisor collect_needs_you finds features with list_cells (live store only) while feature_parked_cells reads the archive too — make both read the same set. Tests red-first for each.
